**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §2.6. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

The rank tells us how many independent directions our feature matrix actually contains. A basis is a minimal set of vectors that spans the relevant space.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
\operatorname{rank}(A)=\dim\bigl(\operatorname{im}(A)\bigr)\leq\min(m,n)
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

Columns (1,0), (0,1), and (1,1) span R^2 but only two are independent. Thus the rank of the 2-by-3 matrix formed by these columns is two. The third column adds no new direction.

## What follows, and what does not

In regression, insufficient column rank prevents a unique ordinary least-squares coefficient vector unless additional constraints or regularisation are introduced.

## Test your reasoning

If a third feature is distance+items, how does it affect rank when both original features are already present?
